Checked direction of dependency edges, empty-predecessor base cases, nonnegative cost domain, and distinction between blocking and pipelined readiness.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Logical operators, partition tasks, execution attempts, outputs, graph versions, and runtime states remain distinct.

evidence: Executed task-graph-invariants with Python 3.14.4 and reproduced the eight-vertex topological order, six readiness levels, total work 19, critical path length 15, maximum level width 2, and four join descendants.
Recomputed the exercise work 15, span 13, three-worker lower bound max(15/3,13)=13, and example lower bound max(100/4,30)=30.

evidence: Re-derived earliest-start and earliest-finish recurrences over a topological order and reconstructed the maximizing predecessor chain.
Derived the ideal runtime lower bound from total worker capacity and the sequential dependency span.
Checked that zero-indegree elimination consumes every vertex exactly when the finite directed graph is acyclic.

evidence: Reviewed empty predecessor sets, unintended cycles, structured cycles, zero-cost vertices, unequal durations, hidden dependencies, partial/pipelined input, missing materialization, long lineage, shared ancestors, dynamic child duplication, and unbounded sources.

Reviewed nondeterminism, mutable sources, unavailable versions, retry and speculation races, partial external effects, late attempts, cancellation, backpressure, adaptive rewrite, worker loss, region loss, and clinical delivery failure.

evidence: Traced graph/operator/task/attempt/output identities, edge contracts, readiness, accepted commit, lineage, materialized cut points, cycle policy, rewrite versions, and effect reconciliation throughout exposition and exercises.

evidence: Reviewed all eight task-graph obligations from semantic identity through operations and review.
